claims.text: Grain refinement in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys will produce a spatially distributed magnetostructural transition.
A spatially distributed magnetostructural transition will broaden the entropy-change profile.
Grain refinement will reduce hysteretic losses during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The initial FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
Magnetron sputtering with enhanced cooling rates can produce a refined or nanocrystalline grain structure.
Grain refinement increases grain-boundary and interfacial area.
A finer nanocrystalline microstructure promotes gradual and spatially inhomogeneous nucleation and growth of the magnetostructural transition.
Additional grain boundaries and interfaces lower the nucleation barrier for the magnetostructural transformation.
Grain boundaries and interfaces provide stress-relief sites.
Interfacial stress relief reduces magnetostructural hysteresis.
The higher surface area of deposited samples improves heat exchange.
Improved heat exchange mitigates the sharpness of the entropy-change profile while preserving a sizable magnetocaloric response.
Refined-grain films will have a broader magnetostructural transition than the baseline.
Refined-grain films will have a lower hysteresis width than the baseline.
Refined-grain films will retain a large entropy change.
Refined-grain deposited samples will exchange heat faster during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Bulk arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons have larger grains, sharp and strongly hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transitions, and limited heat-exchange rates.
The predicted grain-size effects should apply primarily to nanocrystalline samples under low applied fields near the intrinsic transition temperature.
Residual stresses and compositional inhomogeneities may alter the magnitude of the grain-refinement effect.
Failure to observe both transition broadening and reduced hysteresis, or failure of those changes to correlate with measured grain size, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is called as-deposited but is exemplified by arc-melted ingots and melt-spun microribbons, while the intervention creates deposited films and the comparison baseline is alternately described as as-deposited and as bulk arc-melted or melt-spun material.

Grain refinement is treated as increasing the sample surface-to-volume ratio, although it directly increases internal grain-boundary area; external surface-to-volume ratio is primarily controlled by specimen geometry or thickness, which is not independently specified.
